subject: SLO telemetry runbook + customer dashboard access (procurement ask)
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@bluewave.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@bluewave.com
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement questionnaire — metrics access and SLO exception path

Hi Michael,

Thanks for taking our call last week. Procurement at BlueWave is compiling the vendor evidence packet and we have a short set of follow-ups specifically about SLOs and customer-facing metrics:

1) How do you measure uptime and latency SLOs? What exact signals and aggregation windows are used?
2) How are alerts generated (who owns alerting thresholds and runbooks)?
3) Can customers view raw or aggregated telemetry (dashboards, query access, retention windows)?
4) If we need an SLA exception or temporary degradation window (e.g., migration), what is the formal exception request process and typical approval timeline?

We'd appreciate short answers and any existing runbook/document we can attach to our package. Target is to include this in the contract review next week (timeline is tight).

Best,
Alice Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
BlueWave Analytics

[BlueWave logo omitted]
From: michael_grant@redwood.ai <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@bluewave.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — metrics access and SLO exception path

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below and I've attached a one-page runbook (slo_runbook_v1.pdf) that pulls this together for procurement.

1) Measurement: Uptime is computed as percentage of 1-minute checks where the API responds with 2xx within a 1s baseline for our hosted tier. Latency SLOs use p50/p95/p99 over 5-minute sliding windows sampled at request level; rolling windows for reporting are 1h and 30d (for monthly SLA calculations we use calendar-month aggregates).

2) Alerting: Thresholds are defined by product SLO configs in the console and owned by SRE. Alerts are routed to incident channels (PagerDuty for Sev1, Slack #infra-alerts for Sev2) and trigger runbook playbooks. Thresholds are configurable per customer for Dedicated/Private offerings; hosted defaults are documented in the attached runbook.

3) Customer access: Customers get a read-only Grafana dashboard with prebuilt panels (uptime, tail latency, error budget burn). For Dedicated/Private we also offer a query role (Prometheus read) on request. Retention: raw traces/metrics 30 days, aggregated metrics 13 months. If you need longer retention we can discuss an add-on.

4) Exception process: Submit an exception request (email + short form) to exceptions@redwood.ai. SRE reviews within 48 business hours for routine exceptions; approvals that require SLA contract changes go to Product + Legal and typically complete within 5–10 business days depending on complexity. During an approved exception window we provide temporary status page banners and a scoped mitigation plan; documentation required includes start/end times, impacted endpoints, and verification criteria.

Attachments: slo_runbook_v1.pdf (SLO definitions, alert flows, dashboard screenshots)

Next steps: happy to run a 20-min walkthrough of the dashboard if procurement wants to see live panels. Lauren — tagging you for any additional commercial language we should include for the contract. Rishi — any SRE caveats to add?

Thanks,

Michael Grant
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@bluewave.com>, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — metrics access and SLO exception path

Hi Alice — quick commercial clarifications to complement Michael's technical answers:

- Grafana access: we'll provision a tenant-level read-only view for BlueWave on our hosted Grafana; link and SSO instructions included in the grafana-invite-link.txt attachment. If you prefer private/dedicated hosting of dashboards we can include that in the Dedicated proposal.
- Exception approvals: standard procurement language we recommend for contract: "Customer may request temporary SLO exception; Provider will respond within 48 business hours and will document exception period and mitigation steps. Exceptions that materially alter SLA credits require mutual written agreement." Happy to put that clause into redlines if it helps speed review.
- Evidence: the runbook includes sample alert screenshots and the metric names we'll expose (redwood.api.uptime_check, redwood.api.latency_ms.p95).

I'll be on the call Wednesday at 10am PT if you'd like me to cover the contractual wording and evidence.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Contracts & Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@bluewave.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@bluewave.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — metrics access and SLO exception path

Thanks Michael and Lauren — this is exactly what we need. A couple of follow-ups before legal:

- Can you confirm Grafana read-only link will be live for our reviewers by EOD Friday? We need to attach a screenshot + live link to the vendor packet.
- For the exception turnaround: when you say 48 business hours, does that start on submission timestamp or at the next business day? (We have an internal policy that counts calendar hours, so we want to ensure alignment.)

Also please send the grafana link and the runbook PDF as separate attachments for the packet (we need direct files rather than links when possible).

Appreciate the fast response. If everything looks good I'll route to legal for final review.

Best,
Alice
